title: Plate Viewer
description: Turn real object measurements into a plate heatmap, audit individual wells, and test edge and gradient artifacts without modifying the database.
objectives: Open a spaCR measurements database read-only and choose a table, measurement, plate, aggregation, and robust colour scale.
Interpret the plate heatmap alongside edge-effect, row-gradient, and column-gradient diagnostics.
Distinguish low-count blank wells from true zeroes and export the currently filtered well grid.
prerequisite: A measurements database with plate, row, column, and numeric measurement columns.

scenes.narration: Plate Viewer turns any object measurement into a well heatmap and places edge-effect diagnostics beside it. Open it from Results and quality control. The workflow is structurally read-only: spaCR opens the measurements database in query-only mode and writes only an optional exported CSV.
scenes.speech_text: Plate Viewer turns any object measurement into a well heatmap and places edge effect diagnostics beside it. Open it from Results and quality control. The workflow is structurally read only: spacer opens the measurements database in query only mode and writes only an optional exported C S V.

scenes.narration: Drop a measurements database or its run folder, or choose either here. This is the transferred experiment's real database, containing 81,969 measured cells across 196 wells. Plate Viewer reads table names and only the identifier and measurement columns needed for the selected view.
scenes.speech_text: Drop a measurements database or its run folder, or choose either here. This is the transferred experiment's real database, containing eighty one thousand nine hundred sixty nine measured cells across one hundred ninety six wells. Plate Viewer reads table names and only the identifier and measurement columns needed for the selected view.

scenes.narration: Choose the Cell table and a numeric feature. Here we select the mean intensity of channel 1, the endoplasmic-reticulum channel. After the first render, the Plate selector is populated from the data; this database contains plate 1.
scenes.speech_text: Choose the Cell table and a numeric feature. Here we select the mean intensity of channel one, the endoplasmic reticulum channel. After the first render, the Plate selector is populated from the data; this database contains plate one.

scenes.narration: Per well controls how objects collapse to one value. Mean and median summarize the chosen feature, while Count plots object number. The robust 2-to-98-percent colour scale prevents one extreme well from flattening the rest, and Minimum objects per well marks underpowered wells as blank rather than zero.
scenes.speech_text: Per well controls how objects collapse to one value. Mean and median summarize the chosen feature, while Count plots object number. The robust two to ninety eight percent colour scale prevents one extreme well from flattening the rest, and Minimum objects per well marks underpowered wells as blank rather than zero.

scenes.narration: Click Render with Mean, the robust scale, and a minimum of 100 cells. The database query is cached, so later changes to aggregation, colour scale, plate, or minimum count recompute the view without rereading the full feature table.
scenes.speech_text: Click Render with Mean, the robust scale, and a minimum of one hundred cells. The database query is cached, so later changes to aggregation, colour scale, plate, or minimum count recompute the view without rereading the full feature table.

scenes.narration: All 196 measured wells survive. Mean ER intensity has no categorical outer-ring effect, but the real report detects a monotonic row gradient with Spearman rho 0.454. The ring profile and row and column diagnostics keep this spatial trend visible beside the heatmap instead of letting it masquerade as biology.
scenes.speech_text: All one hundred ninety six measured wells survive. Mean E R intensity has no categorical outer ring effect, but the real report detects a monotonic row gradient with Spearman rho zero point four five four. The ring profile and row and column diagnostics keep this spatial trend visible beside the heatmap instead of letting it masquerade as biology.

scenes.narration: Click any well for its exact identifier, object count, aggregated value, and ring position. G07 is an interior well here. This direct mapping is useful for deciding whether an apparent hit belongs to a spatial pattern before opening its fields or crops elsewhere.
scenes.speech_text: Click any well for its exact identifier, object count, aggregated value, and ring position. G zero seven is an interior well here. This direct mapping is useful for deciding whether an apparent hit belongs to a spatial pattern before opening its fields or crops elsewhere.

scenes.narration: Switch Per well to Count. Count ignores the selected intensity value and colors each well by the number of retained cells, which is often the quickest quality-control view for toxicity, segmentation loss, uneven seeding, or edge-dependent growth.
scenes.speech_text: Switch Per well to Count. Count ignores the selected intensity value and colors each well by the number of retained cells, which is often the quickest quality control view for toxicity, segmentation loss, uneven seeding, or edge dependent growth.

scenes.narration: The real count view exposes an outer-ring effect: edge wells contain 14.3 percent more cells than the interior, with Cliff's delta 0.571 and p equal to 0.0003817. The report states the effect direction and magnitude instead of asking you to infer it from colour alone.
scenes.speech_text: The real count view exposes an outer ring effect: edge wells contain fourteen point three percent more cells than the interior, with Cliffs delta zero point five seven one and p equal to zero point zero zero zero three eight one seven. The report states the effect direction and magnitude instead of asking you to infer it from color alone.

scenes.narration: Raise Minimum objects per well to 350 when that count is the minimum evidence required for comparison. The filter is a quality threshold, not an imputation rule: wells below it leave the numeric analysis and become crossed blanks.
scenes.speech_text: Raise Minimum objects per well to three hundred fifty when that count is the minimum evidence required for comparison. The filter is a quality threshold, not an imputation rule: wells below it leave the numeric analysis and become crossed blanks.

scenes.narration: Twenty-eight of the 196 measured wells are now dropped, leaving 168 for the edge test. The outer-ring effect remains detectable at plus 10.5 percent. Crossed cells on the heatmap are missing after filtering; they are never colored as if their value were zero.
scenes.speech_text: Twenty eight of the one hundred ninety six measured wells are now dropped, leaving one hundred sixty eight for the edge test. The outer ring effect remains detectable at plus ten point five percent. Crossed cells on the heatmap are missing after filtering; they are never colored as if their value were zero.

scenes.narration: Click a crossed well to confirm why it is blank. C14 contains 233 measured cells, fewer than the required 350, so the readout reports blank and names the threshold. This makes low support distinguishable from an actual zero count.
scenes.speech_text: Click a crossed well to confirm why it is blank. C fourteen contains two hundred thirty three measured cells, fewer than the required three hundred fifty, so the readout reports blank and names the threshold. This makes low support distinguishable from an actual zero count.

scenes.narration: Click Export well grid CSV to save the current tidy view. Each row retains well identity, object count, displayed value, ring index, and edge flag, so the plate-level result can be audited or replotted outside spaCR without exporting the object-level feature table.
scenes.speech_text: Click Export well grid C S V to save the current tidy view. Each row retains well identity, object count, displayed value, ring index, and edge flag, so the plate level result can be audited or replotted outside spacer without exporting the object level feature table.

scenes.narration: The verified export contains 168 wells, exactly matching the filtered heatmap. A before-and-after SHA-256 check confirms that the source measurements database is byte-identical, completing a read-only plate quality-control pass with a traceable derived table.
scenes.speech_text: The verified export contains one hundred sixty eight wells, exactly matching the filtered heatmap. A before and after S H A two fifty six check confirms that the source measurements database is byte identical, completing a read only plate quality control pass with a traceable derived table.
